cells.tense: The pen is in your hand now, at the edge of what is arriving.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Notice what you'd genuinely rather head toward, then turn and walk one step that way today. No plan, no speech after it.
cells.core:
Something is at the edge of arriving, and it hasn't chosen a shape yet, and you're not forcing one. You can be with it undecided, which is rarer than it sounds — most people settle a thing before they've looked at it. Because you stay available, what's here shows itself first.

What feeds this balance isn't more room; it's wanting clearly. Let yourself know the direction you'd walk if nothing stopped you, and then face that it's what you want. Not a plan. Just the way you'd really go. What's available stays available because you're standing in it on purpose, not because you're steering clear of what you'd choose.
cells.sheetLine: You're open. Say which direction you'd walk.
cells.verb: facing what is arriving before deciding what it will be
cells.place: the threshold where what comes in meets whoever will let it in

cells.tense: You will still be circling this next season, having landed on nothing at all.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: Do something today your own way, no notes and no explaining why. Keep the reasons to yourself and leave the thing done.
cells.core:
You're standing somewhere a lot could start, and the trouble is that all of it stays possible. Nothing gets picked, so nothing gets to exist. From outside it looks like patience; inside it's never quite touching ground, and the longer it runs, the more each pick looks like it might close off the rest.

What's wanted is to do one real thing and let it carry your fingerprints. Choose something you can already do, do it the way you'd do it if nobody watched, and hold the explanation. What gets decided doesn't have to be big. It has to be yours, and finished, so that one of the possibilities stops being a possibility and becomes something that exists in a world other people can see.
cells.sheetLine: Everything's still possible, which is why nothing has happened.

cells.place: the threshold where what comes in meets whoever will let it in

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that is already behind you, and the choice moved on without you.
cells.act: draw the whole arrangement you are inside, with yourself marked on it
cells.ask: On one sheet, sketch loosely how the parts of your life sit around each other, and mark where you are. Look at it once before putting it away.
cells.core:
The openness here isn't closed for lack of wanting; it looks sealed, and you're working from behind glass. Things arrive, and you meet them at arm's length, if at all, so what comes in gets worn down to very little by the time it reaches you. That's not a failure of nerve. It's just what the stance has become.

What loosens it isn't pushing harder at the openness. It's seeing more, from where you already are. Put the whole arrangement on one sheet — the parts of your life and how they sit — and mark yourself in it. Looking longer than you'd like shows you what you're standing inside, and a little more of it becomes visible, and then a little more.

cells.tense: You are answering what arrives as though reacting were the same as meeting it.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Take the next small step without knowing where the one after it goes. You don't need the whole way lit, only the ground your foot lands on.
cells.core:
You're moving through what's arriving, and it looks like there's one way in each time. The choices that are actually yours blend into the ones you'd make the same way whoever was there. From inside, nothing looks missing — reacting feels like responding, and it feels like the usual number of ways in.

What's been driving this isn't a plan. It's habit wearing the shape of one. Set your foot on the next small step — the one already here — and take it with only as much light as that step needs. Not the whole way. Fog is fine. Going this way shows you which turns were yours and which were just the track you kept walking in.
cells.sheetLine: You're reacting, not choosing. One small step, less light.
